name: Blizzard 1230 IV
fits: A1200 only
notes: The example this file was started with, and a real card: the trapdoor accelerator most A1200s ended up with. Its type is what makes it a part rather than a machine.

fields.label: Memory
fields.value: one 72-pin SIMM socket, up to 128 MB at 60-70 ns

fields.label: Provides
fields.value: optional Fast SCSI 2 DMA controller, the Blizzard SCSI Kit IV

name: Sound Blaster 16
fits: any ISA PC
notes: An example of a PC card.

name: BigRAM 2008
notes: Zorro II memory card. Autoconfiguring, so it works in any Zorro machine rather than one model - which is why it is here as the example of a card that fits several. The 2008 is a model number, not a year.

fields.label: Memory
fields.value: 8 MB soldered to the board, sixteen 1M x 4 chips

fields.label: Configurable
fields.value: 2, 4 or 6 MB, to avoid clashing with another card

name: MNT ZZ9000
fits: Zorro II and Zorro III machines; A500 via the ZZ9500CX adapter
notes: Graphics, Ethernet and USB on one Zorro card, built on a Xilinx Zynq XC7Z020 — an FPGA and two ARM cores rather than a fixed graphics chip, so what it does is decided by firmware. Successor to the VA2000. Still made and still supported, which makes it an odd thing to find in a retro catalogue and exactly the kind of card a working Amiga has in it.

fields.label: Chip
fields.value: Xilinx Zynq XC7Z020: 7-series FPGA plus 2x ARM Cortex-A9 @ 666 MHz

fields.label: Resolution
fields.value: up to 1920x1080 — 16-bit at FHD, up to 32-bit below it

fields.label: Video in
fields.value: Amiga native passthrough with AGA scandoubler and flicker-fixer (ZZ9000CX)

fields.label: USB
fields.value: mass storage, mountable as an Amiga drive

fields.label: Firmware
fields.value: BOOT.bin on a FAT32 MicroSD card

fields.label: Driver
fields.value: RTG via Picasso96; needs Kickstart 3.1+ and 68020+

fields.label: Revisions
fields.value: R-1 to R-4; R-1 and R-2 need the trace-cut fix

fields.label: Add-on
fields.value: ZZ9000AX audio card, firmware 1.10 or later

name: Blizzard Turbo Memory
fits: A500 and A2000, into the 68000 socket
notes: A 68000 at twice the clock with room for up to 8 MB beside it, and optional static RAM to hold a copy of Kickstart. It replaces the processor rather than sitting on a bus, so it predates the question of which slot a card belongs in.

fields.label: Memory
fields.value: sixteen DIP sockets, 1 to 8 MB of 256k×4 or 1M×4 at 100 ns

fields.label: Shadow RAM
fields.value: optional 512 kB SRAM for Kickstart remapping

name: Blizzard 1220/4
fits: A1200 only
notes: The cheap end of the Blizzard trapdoor range: memory soldered on rather than socketed, which is why it is 4 MB and stays 4 MB unless the Add-4 board turns up with it.

fields.label: Coprocessor
fields.value: optional PLCC FPU, 68881 @ 14 MHz to 68882 @ 40 MHz

fields.label: Memory
fields.value: 4 MB of 70 ns RAM on board, eight DIP chips

name: Blizzard 1240 ERC & 1260
fits: A1200 only
notes: One board, two names, by which processor was fitted. The 68040s were pulled from used Macs, which is what ERC means. Known not to get on with the Squirrel SCSI interface or with Mikronik towers.

fields.label: Memory
fields.value: one 72-pin SIMM socket, up to 64 MB at 70 ns or faster

fields.label: Memory note
fields.value: single-sided SIMMs only; size detected automatically

fields.label: Provides
fields.value: optional Fast SCSI 2 DMA controller, the Blizzard SCSI Kit IV

name: Blizzard PPC / 603e & 603e Plus
fits: A1200 only
notes: Two processors on one trapdoor board, the 68k running the operating system and the PowerPC running whatever was written for it. The Plus is the one with SCSI. It can be ordered with an empty socket for a 680x0 already owned.

fields.label: Memory
fields.value: two 72-pin SIMM sockets, up to 256 MB at 60 or 70 ns

fields.label: Provides
fields.value: Fast SCSI 2 on the 603e Plus, NCR 53C710

name: Blizzard 2040 ERC & 2060
fits: A2000, into the CPU slot
notes: The A2000 counterpart to the 1240/1260, with SCSI fitted rather than optional and four SIMM sockets instead of one. The 68000 fallback works only on a rev. B A2000.

fields.label: Memory
fields.value: four 72-pin SIMM sockets, up to 128 MB at 70 ns or faster

fields.label: Provides
fields.value: Fast SCSI 2 DMA, 7 MB/s asynchronous and 10 MB/s synchronous

name: Blizzard 4030
fits: A3000 and A4000, into the CPU slot
notes: No memory of its own at all, which sounds like a shortcoming and is the point: it reaches motherboard RAM faster than the A3640 it replaces.

fields.label: Coprocessor
fields.value: optional PGA FPU up to 68882 @ 50 MHz

name: CyberStorm Mk2
fits: A3000 and A4000, into the CPU slot
notes: Sorts any mixture of SIMM sizes into one contiguous block in hardware, so no jumpers decide where memory lands. The optional SCSI module will not fit mechanically in a desktop A3000, and needs an INT2 signal the A3000 CPU slot does not carry.

fields.label: Memory
fields.value: four 72-pin SIMM sockets, up to 128 MB at 70 ns

fields.label: Memory note
fields.value: burst access; 70 ns even with 60 ns SIMMs

fields.label: Provides
fields.value: optional CyberSCSI Mk2, Fast SCSI 2 on a FAS216

name: CyberStorm PPC
fits: A3000 and A4000, into the CPU slot
notes: Particular about how its SIMMs are organised internally: eleven address lines mean 2048×2048 arrays work and 1024×4096 arrays give half the RAM they should. The datasheet settles it, not the size printed on the module.

fields.label: Memory
fields.value: four 72-pin SIMM sockets, up to 128 MB at 60-70 ns, 64-bit interleaved

name: CyberStorm Mk3
fits: A3000 and A4000, into the CPU slot
notes: The CyberStorm PPC board with the PowerPC parts left off, and no way to add them later. The SCSI controller wants an INT2 signal the A3000 CPU slot does not have.

fields.label: Processor
fields.value: 68060 @ 50 MHz, or an empty socket for one already owned

fields.label: Memory
fields.value: four 72-pin SIMM sockets, up to 128 MB at 60-70 ns

name: CyberVision 64
notes: A VL bus chip on a Zorro III card rather than a PCI one behind a bridge, which is how it reaches video memory as quickly as it does. The Roxxler converts planar to chunky.

name: CyberVision 64/3D
fits: Zorro II in an A2000, Zorro III in an A3000 or A4000
notes: Senses which Zorro it is in rather than being ordered for one, which is why it fits both. The scandoubler is a separate module in line with it on the video slot; an MPEG decoder was also offered.

fields.label: Graphics chip
fields.value: S3 ViRGE on a 25 MHz local PCI bus

fields.label: Memory
fields.value: 4 MB of 64-bit page mode DRAM, eight chips

fields.label: Options
fields.value: monitor switch and scandoubler module; MPEG decoder module

fields.label: Interface
fields.value: Zorro II or Zorro III, sensed automatically

fields.label: Autoconfig ID
fields.value: 8512 / 67 on Zorro II, 8512 / 50 on Zorro III

name: BlizzardVision PPC
fits: the Blizzard PPC, in an A1200
notes: Not a slot card. It mounts on the Blizzard PPC and needs that board reflashed first. No passthrough and no monitor switch, so the native modes need a way of their own to reach the screen.

fields.label: Interface
fields.value: expansion slot on the Blizzard PPC

name: CyberVision PPC
fits: the CyberStorm PPC or Mk3, in an A3000 or A4000
notes: The BlizzardVision PPC for the big machines, and the same rule applies: it mounts on the processor board, not in a slot. A rev 1.0 board mounts only vertically, which leaves no room for it in an A3000.

fields.label: Connector
fields.value: 15-pin DSUB, plus 3-pin mini DIN on rev 1.1

fields.label: Interface
fields.value: expansion slot on the CyberStorm PPC or Mk3

name: Fastlane Z3
notes: SCSI and a large amount of memory on one Zorro III card. Sixteen 30-pin sockets, filled four at a time in matching sizes. Works even with a Buster rev. 09.

fields.label: Controller
fields.value: Fast SCSI 2 on a FAS216, 32-bit FIFO, interrupt-driven DMA

fields.label: Memory
fields.value: sixteen 30-pin SIMM sockets, 64 or 256 MB at 60-100 ns

name: Blizzard SCSI Kit IV
fits: the Blizzard 1230 IV and 1240/1260
notes: The optional SCSI module those two boards are described as taking. It carries a second SIMM socket, so fitting it adds memory as well as disks.

fields.label: Controller
fields.value: Fast SCSI 2 DMA on a Qlogic FAS216

fields.label: Memory
fields.value: one further 72-pin SIMM socket, up to 128 MB

fields.label: Interface
fields.value: expansion connector on the host accelerator

name: Commodore A2091
notes: The SCSI card an A2000HD shipped with, and later found in machines it suits badly: it cannot DMA into 32-bit fast RAM, so in an A4000 the driver falls back to programmed I/O and the card crawls. There is an XT IDE controller on it whose connectors were never fitted.

fields.label: Controller
fields.value: Western Digital 33C93, with the A3000's DMAC for transfers

fields.label: Memory
fields.value: sixteen DIP sockets, 0.5, 1 or 2 MB of 256k×4 at 120 ns

fields.label: Connectors
fields.value: internal 50-pin, external DB25; room for a 3.5" disk on the card

fields.label: Firmware
fields.value: 16 kB autoboot ROM; Kickstart 1.3 or later, rev 7.0 for 68040 machines

name: Commodore A590
fits: A500, on the side expansion port
notes: The A2091 design in a box beside the A500, with its own power supply. Both SCSI and XT IDE work at once. No passthrough on the expansion port, so it is the last thing on that side of the machine.

fields.label: Controller
fields.value: Western Digital 33C93 DMA SCSI, plus 8-bit XT IDE

fields.label: Memory
fields.value: sixteen DIP sockets, 0.5, 1 or 2 MB of 256k×4 at 120 ns

fields.label: Connectors
fields.value: internal 50-pin SCSI, internal 40-pin XT IDE, external DB25

fields.label: Power
fields.value: its own supply, switched on with the A500
